Thought: I need to determine the reactivity order of these compounds in nucleophilic acyl substitution. Let me first identify what each SMILES notation represents and then analyze their reactivity.

1. N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N[C@H](CO)CC1=CC=CC=C1)=O - This appears to be a peptide/amide structure
2. O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1 - This is an acyl chloride (cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride)
3. O=C([O-])C1=CC=CC=C1 - This is a carboxylate anion (benzoate)

For nucleophilic acyl substitution reactions, the reactivity depends on the leaving group ability. The better the leaving group, the more reactive the compound.

The general reactivity order for acyl compounds in nucleophilic acyl substitution is:
- Acyl chlorides (most reactive)
- Anhydrides
- Esters
- Amides (least reactive)
- Carboxylates (generally not reactive as they are already the product of nucleophilic attack)

So from least to most reactive:
- Carboxylate (O=C([O-])C1=CC=CC=C1) - least reactive as it's already negatively charged
- Amide (N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N[C@H](CO)CC1=CC=CC=C1)=O) - amides are relatively unreactive
- Acyl chloride (O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1) - most reactive due to the good leaving group (Cl-)

Therefore, the correct ordering from least to most reactive is:
O=C([O-])C1=CC=CC=C1, N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N[C@H](CO)CC1=CC=CC=C1)=O, O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1

This matches option C.
